lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 77, which stops the screenshot audit from running when CI took no shots.
It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The visual-verify skill gets a new Step 0, fed by the pr-digest agent.
First, the skill takes a digest of the pull request, for its current head.
The digest says whether build and verify ran their steps, ran No code changed, or skipped them.
The skill looks for that one step, never just a missing manifest.
When both ran it, the skill says not needed, and posts no verdict or comment.
Otherwise the preflight and the audit run exactly as before.
On a docs-only pull request, CI takes no shots, so the old skill found nothing and sent the PR to the owner.
The skill can't call GitHub itself, so it asks pr-digest, which already reads the build's jobs.
The digest must match the head. While build or verify is still running, the skill waits and asks again.
A verify run that skipped by mistake still ends inconclusive, so nothing passes silently.
For every other run, Step 1 and the audit are unchanged.
The PR changes the skill's instructions and the digest agent's, plus this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert the PR. Agents then fall back on the rule in CLAUDE.md alone.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows the summary script, which already says not needed, and the merge rule in CLAUDE.md.
A search confirmed the step's name is the same in the summary script and the build workflow.
This pull request's own CI run is itself a no-code run.
The skill's new behaviour on later pull requests can't run before the merge.
A fresh review agent found six problems before the first push, and all six were fixed.
The digest's wording now says that both the job and its step must succeed.
The check moved to its own Step 0, so the skill no longer contradicts itself.
The digest must match the head, and a run in progress is waited for.
CI's own review is in its comment on the pull request.
After the merge, the next docs-only pull request and the next code one show it working.
On this pull request, the summary's audit row already says not needed.
Part 3. What comes later.
No issue builds on this one. The next docs-only pull request merges without an audit ask.
In short: no screenshots, no audit, and no needless trip to the owner.
